question: Under the Regulating Act of 1773, the King-in-Council created a Supreme Court in which of the following places?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcutta**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under the** Regulating Act of 1773,** the Supreme Court of Judicature was established in **Calcutta**
 
• This court** replaced the Mayor’s Court of Calcutta** and served as British India’s highest court from 1774 until 1862.
 
• The Regulating Act **aimed to improve the management of judicial functions in India,**
 
 
• And the establishment of the Supreme Court was a significant step in achieving that goal.
 
 
 
• The Supreme Court at Calcutta had both **civil and criminal jurisdiction**
 
• It was **responsible for administering the British legal system** in India.
 
• **Sir Elijah Impey** served as the first **Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Calcutta**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• ** Regulating Act of 1773****​**

 
 
• The 'Regulating Act' of 1773 was passed by the British Parliament to control the territories of the East India Company majorly in Bengal.
 
• This act was passed due to the misgovernment by the British East India government that introduced a situation of bankruptcy and the government had to interfere with the affairs of the Company.
 
• The Regulating Act was passed in the British Parliament in June 1773.
 
• The act provided for the appointment of a Governor-General along with four Councillors in the Presidency of Fort William (Calcutta), jointly called the Governor-General in Council.
